notes: Claims and judges that exist. (1) every body of every folder, INBOX first, newest first, each UID once, resume after a stop: core/crates/engine/tests/engine_sync_full_r1.rs:166 a_the_crawl_stores_every_body_inbox_first_newest_first_and_resumes_after_a_stop (asserts INBOX 16..25 first, batches of at most 10 newest first, no UID twice, resume reads fewer rows). The source is an in-process FakeSource (engine_sync_full_r1.rs, `production`), so this is not a socket-level proof of 'one connection'; the crawl code is core/crates/engine/src/crawl.rs (module consts at :20-30; the hold at :29 CRAWL_RECHECK_MS). (2) in batches: same test (BODY_PREFETCH_BATCH), and core/crates/engine/tests/engine_body_r1.rs:203 d_the_prefetch_stores_the_newest_bodies_in_batches_and_repairs_raw_previews and :232 d_after_a_fetch_the_newest_bodies_arrive_unasked. (3) paused on battery or thermal pressure: engine_sync_full_r1.rs:315 d_battery_and_heat_hold_the_crawl_and_release_it (the crawl makes no server call under the floor or under serious heat), and :500 k_the_pause_is_readable_by_its_reason. The reader asked whether the body download uses the crawl hold at crawl.rs:29: the hold is read by the crawl loop itself (crawl.rs, `BackgroundPause` at :53 and the recheck constant at :29), so the crawl, which is the every-folder download, is the part that pauses; the older newest-bodies prefetch of engine_body_r1 (bodies.rs:3) is not paused by battery (unverified: not traced). (4) kept in whoosh.sqlite: engine_sync_full_r1.rs:166 reads the stored body back through core.store().body_parts and the relaunch half re-reads it; engine_body_r1.rs:149 e_a_downloaded_body_is_served_after_a_relaunch_without_the_network. (5) the view and acts stay under 50 ms while the crawl runs on a 300 ms server: :223 b_a_view_or_an_act_answers_under_50_ms_while_the_crawl_runs_on_a_300_ms_server (median over 5 calls, printed; NOT JUDGED above load 12, in which case the run still prints but is not a pass: the lead must run it on a quiet machine and read the lines, hence --nocapture). (gap-engine-tests, 2026-11-11) proof 1 is new: core/crates/engine/tests/engine_crawl_wire.rs. It states two limits of its own: 'one-connection' is asserted as at most 2 sessions open at once on the fake (the sync's IDLE session plus one), the number the gap text asked for; the assertion is the first thing to read if the real count is higher (the test prints the measured number in its PASS line). Written, not run. (tail-realcore, 2026-11-12) `--slice-crawl` (checks/realcore-check.py: drive_crawl, judge_crawl, main_slice_crawl) serves INBOX 25, Archive 15, Sent 10 (realcore_mailfake.CRAWL_PLAN, load_crawl_mail) from a server that now records every whole-message fetch with its connection and folder (`Mail.body_fetches`) and the most sessions open at once (`Mail.max_sessions`). The engine's own figures are read from `core state reply/progress` (messages, bodies, indexed per account and folder). Like engine_crawl_wire.rs it asserts the highest uid of each INBOX fetch falls call by call and at most 2 sessions open at once: if the real run reads higher, those two assertions are the first thing to read. `--paused` is its own run (the plain run is its control): the hook is read only if the shell does not send other conditions after launch (BackgroundEngineLive sends the Mac's real reading at start); the case prints the shell's own `mac-main.background` row beside its verdict. The plain run prints two NOT JUDGED cases (meaning, indexed count) unless WHOOSH_EMBED_WEIGHTS names the lead's model folder; proof 3's pass line therefore asks for the five crawl cases only. Written and self-tested, not run on a bundle. (perf-archive round 5, 2026-11-12) piece (3) is built: perf/footprint.py `crawl` (outer_crawl, inside_crawl, crawl_judge, crawl_summary, crawl_phase) launches the rig copy on the REAL engine through scripts/launch-one.sh against the loopback server of --slice-crawl (realcore_mailfake.start, load_crawl_mail; the account is added by checks/realcore-check.py mv_add_account, read through importlib, never copied), samples the physical footprint and CPU seconds every 0.5 s with the engine's reply/progress, and prints per phase (download, then index with a model folder) `PASS|OVER|NOT JUDGED crawl-<phase>-memory-peak` against RSS_IDLE_MAX_MB + EMBED_INDEX_CEILING_MB and `crawl-<phase>-cpu-average` against CRAWL_CPU_MAX_PCT (NOT JUDGED until the ledger holds that row; also above PERF_LOAD_MAX at the end). Proof 7 is the lead's run (give WHOOSH_EMBED_WEIGHTS for the index phase; without it the index rows read NOT JUDGED and only the download is judged); proof 8 its selftest (11 crawl cases, one a broken copy that takes the median and hides a peak); the mutant on proof 8 replaces max by the median in crawl_judge. The plan is 100 small messages: a reading of the crawl's machinery, not of a large mailbox. Proposed ledger row (docs/lanes/perf-archive.md Round 5): CRAWL_CPU_MAX_PCT, the download phase's average CPU from proof 7's first quiet run; the lead sets it.
